27997.description:
Job Type:
Permanent
About us
K92 Mining Limited are the owners the high-grade Kainantu Gold Mine in Eastern Highlands Province. Since commencing operations in 2016, we have delivered consistent production growth. More importantly, we have contributed significantly to the economy of Papua New Guinea, more than 90% of our employees and contractors are from PNG and our local education and skills development initiatives which include scholarships, traineeships and adult literacy programs continue to bring significant benefit the communities in which we operate.
We are now transforming the operation with a new 1.2 mtpa process plant as well as extensive construction and expansion across site that will see us triple the output from our mine by 2027. In addition to our ongoing production success, we have an extensive exploration programme across our highly prospective tenement, making K92 a great place to build a long-term career.
About the role
In this role you will assist the Raisebore Driller with the safe and efficient setup, operation, and maintenance of raise drilling activities while maintaining a safe working environment.
Key Accountabilities
Key accountabilities of this position include.
Assist with moving, handling, and setting up drill rods for raise drilling operations.
Support the Raisebore Driller in daily drilling tasks and operational requirements.
Monitor drilling activities and assist as required to ensure safe and efficient operation.
Conduct pre-start checks and greasing of the raise drill.
Clean, inspect, and grease drill rod threads to maintain equipment integrity.
Monitor and operate the 90kW pump used for drilling fluids.
Clean and maintain the drill rig, associated equipment, and surrounding work area.
Operate Light Vehicles (LV) in underground environments.
Operate Telehandler equipment where required.
Operate Volvo IT120 (forks and basket) in accordance with site procedures.
Use basic hand tools safely and effectively.
Maintain high standards of housekeeping in all work areas.
Follow all site safety procedures and instructions.
Work collaboratively as part of a team to achieve operational goals.
About You
It is requirement of the position that the incumbent possesses the following.
Valid driver’s licence (suitable for site requirements)
Ability to work in a physically demanding environment
Machinery operation tickets (LV, Telehandler, IT Loader)
Previous underground or mining experience.
Grade 12 Level education.
Strong safety awareness and commitment to safe work practices.
Ability to perform manual labour tasks consistently and safely.
Capability to follow instructions and implement them correctly.
Good teamwork and communication skills.
Basic mechanical aptitude and familiarity with hand tools.
Ability to perform duties with minimum supervision.
Able to communicate effectively at all levels.
Life at K92
K92 is an Equal Opportunity Employer, our commitment is to respect the rights of every individual to work to their highest potential, free from discrimination.  Our values of Collaboration, Accountability, Respect for others, Excellence and Safety are at the core of everything we do, and they are the foundation upon which our success has been built.
Our camp is well managed and provides residents with good, healthy meals made from locally sourced fresh produce as well as internet, cable tv and a gymnasium.
At K92, we want all employees to share in our success, so as well as a competitive salary, employees also participate in our long- and short-term incentive plans, we also provide employees with access to savings incentive programs, medical assistance and the option to salary sacrifice for certain expenses.
In addition to all of this, employees can also access our Wellbeing and employee assistance programs whilst working a friendly roster.
THIS POSITION IS OPEN ONLY TO CANDIDATES WHO HAVE THE RIGHT TO LIVE & WORK IN PNG WITHOUT SPONSORSHIP

27985.description:
Work in a supportive environment that fosters professional growth and leadership
Join one of Papua New Guinea's leading financial services organisations.
Drive the growth of consumer lending, sales, and credit operations.
The Company
Our client is a leader within their niche market who is committed to delivering quality financial services and providing innovative, customer-focused solutions that support individuals, businesses and communities.
The Role
Reporting directly to the Head of Credit, the Senior Manager – Consumer Finance/Lending is a key operational and commercial leadership role within the business unit. You will provide strategic and operational leadership across the full consumer lending portfolio, including microfinance, SME lending, personal lending, credit administration and recoveries.
As an experienced operational generalist, you will lead three direct-report Managers responsible for consumer sales, credit administration and collections functions. Working closely with executive leadership, you will drive portfolio growth, optimise lending processes, strengthen credit risk management and enhance the overall customer experience.
Key Responsibilities
Lead the consumer finance portfolio, overseeing personal lending, SME credit and retail finance products.
Lead and mentor three functional Managers responsible for sales, credit administration and recoveries teams across a national network.
Develop and execute lending strategies to grow market share, improve sales performance and maintain strong credit practices.
Implement effective recovery strategies to minimise non-performing loans (NPLs), manage credit risk and ensure regulatory compliance.
Partner with the Head of Credit and executive leadership team to deliver business unit KPIs, strategic initiatives and operational improvements.
Qualifications, Skills & Experience
Bachelor’s degree in business, Banking, Finance or a related discipline.
Minimum of 5years’ senior experience in consumer lending, retail banking or credit management within the financial services sector.
Broad experience across consumer sales, collections, account management, credit administration and business development.
Demonstrated ability to lead multi-level teams, coach managers and drive performance across multi-site operations.
Strong commercial, analytical and risk management capability, with a sound understanding of credit frameworks, governance and Papua New Guinea’s regulatory requirements.
To apply for this position, interested candidates are asked to submit:
A cover letter addressing key criteria of the role
An updated CV in Microsoft Word format, outlining employment history, educational qualifications, and listing three referees (referees will only be contacted if shortlisted)
Our client's priority is to provide opportunities to high performing Papua New Guineans for this position.  Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.

About the role
As our site continues to grow with production doubling in 2026, we have created a new role that will oversee the surface mobile maintenance planning function.
In this role you will be responsible for the effective planning, scheduling, and coordination of maintenance activities to optimise equipment performance and reliability. Utilising Pronto as the core CMMS, you will be charged with forecasting component requirements, tracking critical equipment metrics, and ensuring efficient resource allocation. This role plays a key part in minimising equipment downtime through structured planning, monitoring, and continuous improvement initiatives.
Key Accountabilities
Key accountabilities of this position include.
Develop and implement maintenance schedules for both planned and corrective maintenance activities to ensure equipment reliability and operational efficiency.
Utilise Pronto to track work orders, manage maintenance backlogs, and ensure timely completion of tasks.
Coordinate with procurement and logistics teams to secure the availability of spare parts and components, reducing delays in maintenance activities.
Provide training on best practices in condition monitoring, failure analysis, and equipment tracking to enhance workforce capabilities.
Track and forecast critical component requirements to prevent unscheduled downtime, while monitoring component life cycles and managing replacements in alignment with predictive maintenance strategies.
Develop and track key performance indicators (KPIs) to analyse equipment performance and reliability. These include Mean Time Between Failures (MTBF), Mean Time to Repair (MTTR), Mean Time to Damage (MTTD), Mean Time to Repair Damage Event (MTTRD), Utilisation (U), Utilisation of Availability (UofA), and overall Availability %. By analysing failure trends, implement corrective actions to enhance equipment reliability and reduce unplanned breakdowns.
Work closely with reliability engineers and technicians to implement condition-based monitoring strategies, utilising data analytics tools such as Power BI and Excel to assess equipment health and performance trends. Investigate failures and recommend preventive actions to mitigate future risks.
Coordinate with procurement teams to ensure timely acquisition of parts and components while maintaining optimal stock levels to minimise excess inventory costs.
Conduct regular inventory reviews, perform stock adjustments, and ensure accurate inventory records within Pronto, updating them as required based on usage trends.
Develop and maintain accurate machine Bills of Materials (BOMs) within Pronto for effective parts tracking.
Ensure BOMs remain up to date with equipment modifications and upgrades, enabling efficient maintenance planning.
Prepare structured reports and dashboards using Power BI and Excel to provide insights into maintenance performance, downtime trends, and cost analysis.
Maintain accurate maintenance records and generate data-driven insights for continuous improvement.
Present daily, weekly, and monthly KPI reports while also preparing and maintaining quarterly and annual mobile plant maintenance forecasts.
Contribute to the annual maintenance budgeting process and monthly cost reviews to optimise financial planning and resource allocation.
Ensure health and safety, and environmental performance meets or exceeds company and regulatory requirements.
Ensure all personnel operating in the mining area meet the legislative requirements and hold the appropriate qualifications.

Job Type:
Permanent
About us
K92 Mining Limited are the owners the high-grade Kainantu Gold Mine in Eastern Highlands Province. Since commencing operations in 2016, we have delivered consistent production growth. More importantly, we have contributed significantly to the economy of Papua New Guinea, more than 90% of our employees and contractors are from PNG and our local education and skills development initiatives which include scholarships, traineeships and adult literacy programs continue to bring significant benefit the communities in which we operate.

About the role
Joining our growing exploration department, you will act as the operational bridge between the geologists who plan and direct exploration programmes and the field and drilling personnel who implement them. Reporting to Superintendent Exploration, the role receives day-to-day technical instruction from programme geologists, coordinates ground-level execution with drilling supervisors and field crews, and supervises sampling, logistics and safety compliance.
Key Accountabilities
Key accountabilities of this position include.
Receive priorities, locations, methods, sequence and quality requirements from the responsible geologist and translate them into clear daily field tasks.
Coordinate daily interfaces among geologists, drilling supervisors, survey, contractors, Senior Field Assistants and field crews.
Monitor work against approved plans, report progress and variances, and obtain geological direction before changing scope, location or technical method.
Prepare crew allocations, rosters, access, communications, equipment, consumables and daily field reports.
Coordinate drill-site readiness, including access, collar pegging, pad and sump preparation, drainage, water, lighting, sample areas, environmental controls and rehabilitation.
Liaise with geology, survey and the drilling supervisor during rig moves and set-up to confirm planned collar, dip, azimuth and site requirements.
Observe drilling progress, core or sample recovery, water management, housekeeping and field safety; communicate issues to the drilling supervisor and geologist for action.
Coordinate core and drill-sample movement, metre marking, orientation support, photography, registration and secure delivery without loss, contamination or mix-up.
Check shift records, metres, downtime, consumable usage and contractor dockets for completeness before submission.
Supervise soil, stream-sediment, rock-chip, channel, trench and other sampling to the geologist's approved locations, spacing, depth and methods.
Ensure correct sample IDs, coordinates, descriptions, weights, bags, tags and seals, and maintain Chain-of-Custody through dispatch.
Verify standards, blanks, duplicates and other QA/QC samples at the required frequency; report errors and coordinate corrective or repeat work as directed by geology.
Reconcile physical samples with paper and digital registers, review dispatch documents and confirm laboratory receipt.
Coordinate mapping and survey support, including traverses, outcrop or trench preparation, photographs, measurements and accurate location records.
Lead pre-starts, toolbox meetings, Take 5/JSA activities and field inspections; reinforce required procedures and exercise stop-work authority where conditions are unsafe.
Report hazards, incidents, environmental issues and community or access concerns promptly and support corrective actions.
Maintain emergency communications, first-aid and evacuation readiness, and coordinate drills and field response arrangements.
Coordinate mobilisation, camps, vehicle or helicopter loads, fuel, water, tools, sampling supplies, communications and inventory.
Ensure equipment pre-starts, basic maintenance, defect reporting, waste control, spill prevention and progressive rehabilitation are completed.
Supervise and coach the Senior Field Assistant, Field Assistants and local labour in safe field practices, sampling quality, equipment care, reporting and work discipline.
Maintain regular communication with programme geologists and the Superintendent Exploration on progress, field conditions, risks, delays and resource needs.
Respect the separate accountabilities of geology, drilling contractors and support functions; facilitate coordination rather than assume technical control of their work.
Recommend practical improvements to field safety, logistics, sample quality, productivity and procedures.
About You
To be considered for this role, it is essential that you
Grade 12 education or equivalent experience; a certificate in exploration, mining, geology, safety or frontline supervision is desirable.
Current first-aid certificate and valid field-appropriate driver licence are desirable
At least 8 years of mineral exploration field experience, including experience leading field crews.
Practical experience with drilling support, drill-site logistics, core or sample handling, geochemical sampling, QA/QC and Chain-of-Custody.
Sound understanding of the separate roles of programme geologists, drilling supervisors/contractors and field support personnel.
Competence with GPS units, field records, sample registers, basic survey support, daily reporting and field equipment.
Strong field HSE, environmental and emergency-response awareness and ability to work in remote conditions.
Ability to plan and coordinate work, coach diverse crews, communicate clearly and escalate issues appropriately.
Physically and mentally fit for remote fieldwork; able to speak, read and write English. Tok Pisin or local language capability is advantageous.

Our values of Collaboration, Accountability, Respect for others, Excellence and Safety are at the core of everything we do, and they are the foundation upon which our success has been built.

27108.description:
Job Type:
Permanent
About us
K92 Mining Limited are the owners the high-grade Kainantu Gold Mine in Eastern Highlands Province. Since commencing operations in 2016, we have delivered consistent production growth. More importantly, we have contributed significantly to the economy of Papua New Guinea, more than 90% of our employees and contractors are from PNG and our local education and skills development initiatives which include scholarships, traineeships and adult literacy programs continue to bring significant benefit the communities in which we operate.
We are now transforming the operation with a new 1.2 mtpa process plant as well as extensive construction and expansion across site that will see us triple the output from our mine by 2027. In addition to our ongoing production success, we have an extensive exploration programme across our highly prospective tenement, making K92 a great place to build a long-term career.
About the role
This position is responsible for the service and maintenance of fixed plant equipment in a safe and appropriate manner. You will ensure a preventative maintenance schedule is adhered to as well as perform reactive maintenance when equipment breaks down to ensure downtime of machinery is minimized.
Key Accountabilities
Maintain and repair fixed plant equipment onsite in a safe, responsible and timely and effective manner ensuring all Fixed Plant and K92 mining standards are met.
Oversee installation, operation, repairs, and maintenance of the Fixed Plant equipment and infrastructures.
Maintain all plant equipment and ensure all planning and scheduling maintenance activities are performed safely and more effectively.
Assist the Maintenance Foreman in performing preventative maintenance programs, perform routine maintenance and enforces statutory requirements and assist to create a zero-base safety culture.
Ensure safe work standards and practices in accordance with mine safety regulations for all tasks performed.
The successful completion of daily work to meet quality standards and deadlines.
Reporting faults and hazards and respond to routine emergency calls for repair and service within the mine site area.
Monitoring and assessment of plant and equipment.
Exercise due care and attention to work in a safe and efficient manner.
Assist in supervising and on-job training for Apprentices and Trade Assistance.
Willingness to assist other trades as and when required.
About You
To be considered for this role, you will have certificates from a recognized Tertiary institution or technical training program in a maintenance trade or completion of a recognized apprenticeship program, or combination of the two.
Trade Certificate Fitting & Machinery / Mechanical Fitting.
Sound knowledge of all Processing Plant Equipment or similar.
Possess the ability to troubleshoot and perform root cause analysis (particularly in diagnosis and fault finding).
Must be a self-starter, and very resourceful, with the ability to find solutions to problems to ensure the equipment availability is maintained and the ability to live in a remote environment with limited facilities.
Flexible, adaptable and be a team player.
Good working knowledge of the principles and practices of OH&S and Fixed Plant.
Be flexible and adaptable to the needs of the business and ability to work harmoniously as part of the team.
Life at K92
K92 is an Equal Opportunity Employer, our commitment is to respect the rights of every individual to work to their highest potential, free from discrimination.  Our values of Collaboration, Accountability, Respect for others, Excellence and Safety are at the core of everything we do, and they are the foundation upon which our success has been built.
Our camp is well managed and provides residents with good, healthy meals made from locally sourced fresh produce as well as internet, cable tv and a gymnasium.
At K92, we want all employees to share in our success, so as well as a competitive salary, employees also participate in our long- and short-term incentive plans, we also provide employees with access to savings incentive programs, medical assistance and the option to salary sacrifice for certain expenses.
In addition to all of this, employees can also access our Wellbeing and employee assistance programs whilst working a friendly roster.

28171.description:
With more than 40 years of experience working in PNG, World Vision International Papua New Guinea (WVIPNG) focuses on helping the most vulnerable children and adults experience fullness of life.  Inspired by our Christian faith, WVPNG has an exciting opportunity for someone who may be looking for a change and wants to become part of a dynamic team helping vulnerable people and communities.
World Vision International Papua New Guinea (WVIPNG) has exciting opportunity for those of you who want a change and want to become part of a dynamic team. We are currently looking for suitable, qualified, experienced, and highly motivated professional to fill the role of
Community Facilitator
to be based in
Arawa, Bougainville Area Program.
PURPOSE OF THE POSITION
The Community Facilitator leads frontline engagement—mobilizing communities, facilitating participatory planning and learning, and ensuring inclusive, accountable implementation of WOVEN Phase 2 activities. The role strengthens community ownership, promotes gender and disability inclusion, and supports consistent data capture, reporting, and adaptive management. The community Facilitator should ensure understanding of local culture and governance structures.
MAJOR ROLES AND RESPONSIBILITIES
1.
Community Mobilization & Engagement
Organize and facilitate village-level meetings, focus groups, and participatory planning (e.g., community action plans, small group training, and learning sessions).
Build trusted relationships with community leaders, women’s groups, youth, people with disabilities, farmer groups, savings groups, and other local structures.
Support community awareness on project goals, roles, accountability mechanisms, and safeguarding.
2.
Facilitation of Training & Learning
Deliver or co-facilitate training (e.g., financial literacy, savings groups, inclusive livelihoods, gender and social inclusion, basic nutrition/household practices) using approved curricula and adult-learning methods.
Coach/supervise community volunteers/lead facilitators to sustain activities and learning cycles.
Ensure training is accessible and culturally appropriate (language, timing, venue, materials).
3.
Inclusion, Safeguarding & Accountability
Mainstream gender, disability inclusion, and child safeguarding across all activities.
Establish and maintain feedback, complaints, and response mechanisms at community level.
Proactively identify and mitigate risks (including protection concerns), escalating per protocol.
4.
Partnerships & Coordination
Coordinate with ward/village leaders, ABG/local government officers, church networks, and civil society actors to align efforts and avoid duplication.
Participate in district/ward coordination forums and contribute to joint planning where relevant.
Support linkages to market actors, financial service providers, and relevant services.
5.
Monitoring, Data & Reporting
Collect attendance, activity, and outcome data (including sex- and disability-disaggregated data) using project tools.
Conduct regular community follow-up, household visits, and simple outcome verification.
Prepare concise weekly/monthly field reports, success stories, lessons learned, and case studies.
Feed community insights into adaptive management and quality improvement plans.
6.
Logistics & Compliance
Plan field schedules, manage session materials, and coordinate transport with the project team.
Adhere to WVI organizational policies (safeguarding, anti-fraud/corruption, data protection, safety & security).
Support procurement and asset use at community level per project guidelines
EDUCATIONAL QUALIFICATION/SKILLS, KNOWLEDGE & EXPERIENCE
Tertiary qualification (certificate, diploma, or degree) in Community Development, Social Work, Public Policy, Education, Agriculture/Livelihoods, or related field.
Minimum 2–3 years’ experience in community facilitation within PNG, preferably Bougainville.
Experience in financial literacy/savings groups, gender inclusion, nutrition, agriculture, or resilience programming.
Experience with safeguarding, protection referral pathways, and accountability mechanisms.
Basic digital literacy (smartphone/tablet data entry, WhatsApp/Teams coordination).
Proven experience delivering training courses using participatory and adult-learning approaches.
Experience working with diverse groups (women, youth, people with disabilities) and local leadership structures.
Basic monitoring and reporting skills; comfortable with data collection tools (paper or digital).
Fluency in Tok Pisin and/or local Bougainville languages; good written and spoken English.
Familiarity with ABG coordination processes and ward-level governance.
A competitive salary, benefits, and career development opportunity will be offered commensurate with relevant experience, knowledge, and qualifications.

strong research skills to keep content accurate and logically sound.

Experience delivering training to external, fee-paying clients.

PNG Air, renowned for its extensive network covering over 26 destinations throughout Papua New Guinea, operates the largest fleet of ATR 72-600 & ATR 42-600 series aircraft in the region. As the Airline of Choice, we're committed to delivering a world-class experience with competitive fares, unparalleled cargo rates, and a focus on safety and on-time performance for our valued customers and stakeholders.
REVENUE ACCOUNTING MANAGER
PNG Air is seeking a suitably qualified and experienced
Revenue Accounting Manager
to join its Finance Department based in Port Moresby.
Reporting to the
Chief Financial Officer
, the
Revenue Accounting Manager
is responsible for the integrity, completeness and accuracy of all scheduled passenger (RPT) revenue recognized by PNG Air. The role ensures all passenger, charter, freight, ancillary and interline revenues are accurately accounted for in accordance with International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS), company policies and aviation industry best practice.
The position leads the Revenue Accounting team and is responsible for ensuring timely month-end revenue close, reconciliation of passenger revenue systems, minimizing revenue leakage, strengthening internal controls and delivering meaningful financial information to management to support commercial and operational decision making.
The Revenue Accounting Manager acts as the finance custodian of airline revenue and works closely with Commercial, Sales, Airport Operations, Digital, Call Centre, Finance, Treasury, IT and external service providers to ensure the Company's revenue streams are accurately recorded and protected.
KEY RESPONSIBILITIES
Revenue Accounting
Manage the end-to-end passenger revenue accounting function.
Ensure timely and accurate recognition of passenger, charter, freight ancillary and related revenues.
Review and approve revenue journals, reconciliations and month-end reporting.
Ensure compliance with IFRS, company policies and aviation industry standards.
Revenue Controls & Reconciliations
Oversee reconciliation of revenue systems, banking settlements and the General Ledger.
Investigate and resolve revenue discrepancies and unreconciled items.
Strengthen internal controls to minimise revenue leakage and financial risk.
Financial Reporting
Deliver timely monthly revenue reports and management analysis.
Monitor revenue trends, key performance indicators and operational impacts.
Provide recommendations to improve financial performance and reporting accuracy.
Systems & Process Improvement
Support implementation and enhancement of revenue accounting systems.
Identify opportunities to automate processes and improve efficiency.
Participate in system testing and implementation of new airline technology.
Leadership
Lead, coach and develop the Revenue Accounting team.
Allocate work, monitor performance and foster continuous improvement.
Promote collaboration across Finance and operational departments.
Stakeholder Management
Work closely with Commercial, Sales, Operations, Treasury, Accounts Receivable, IT, Internal Audit and external service providers.
Support internal and external audit requirements.
Provide technical advice on revenue accounting matters.
QUALIFICATIONS/EXPERIENCES
Essential
Bachelor's Degree in Accounting, Finance or Commerce.
Qualified PNG CPA or equivalent professional accounting qualification.
Minimum three years' experience in revenue accounting, financial accounting or a similar finance management role.
Strong analytical, reconciliation and financial reporting skills.
Advanced Microsoft Excel skills.
Desirable
Experience within the aviation industry.
Knowledge of airline Passenger Service Systems (PSS), Revenue Accounting Systems and IATA processes.
Experience with ERP systems such as Sage or equivalent.
If you feel you meet our requirements and are interested, we would like to hear from you. Send your application in only one PDF file to:
[email protected]

Friday 31
st
August 2026
Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.
We are an equal opportunity employer.

Port Moresby, Papua New Guinea
Help shape the future of infrastructure and sustainable development across Papua New Guinea and the Pacific.
MC Infrastructure is seeking an experienced
Environmental Consultant
to join our growing team in Port Moresby.
This is an opportunity to work on some of the region's most significant infrastructure, urban development, mining, energy, transport, and government projects, while helping deliver practical environmental outcomes that improve communities and protect the natural environment.
We are looking for someone who enjoys a mix of field work, technical reporting, project management, and client interaction. Most importantly, we are looking for someone who wants to grow with our business.
For the right person, this role has a genuine pathway into a senior leadership or management position as our environmental services team continues to expand.
About the role
Working within our multidisciplinary engineering and advisory business, you will lead environmental assessment projects across Papua New Guinea and the Pacific region.
You will be responsible for delivering high quality environmental services while working alongside engineers, planners, surveyors, geotechnical specialists, and project managers.
Your work will include:
Environmental Impact Assessments (EIA)
Environmental Management Plans (EMP)
Environmental and social due diligence
Site inspections and field investigations
Stakeholder and community engagement
Environmental approvals and regulatory liaison
Project management and client communication
Technical report writing and review
Coordination of multidisciplinary project teams
Supporting business development and proposal preparation
About you
You are someone who enjoys taking ownership of projects and producing work to a high professional standard.
You will ideally have:
Approximately 5 to 7 years' experience in environmental consulting or more
Experience delivering environmental assessments for infrastructure, mining, transport, energy or development projects
Strong technical report writing skills
Experience managing projects, budgets and client relationships
Excellent organisational and communication skills
A practical approach to solving environmental challenges
A willingness to undertake field work throughout Papua New Guinea and the Pacific
A degree in Environmental Science, Environmental Management or a related discipline
Experience working within Papua New Guinea or developing countries will be highly regarded but is not essential.
Why join MC Infrastructure?
We are building one of the South Pacific's leading multidisciplinary infrastructure and development consultancies.
Our projects are diverse, technically interesting, and make a genuine difference to the communities in which we work.
We offer:
A diverse portfolio of projects across Papua New Guinea and the Pacific
A supportive multidisciplinary team
Genuine responsibility from day one
Opportunities to travel throughout the region
Exposure to major infrastructure and development projects
A clear pathway into senior leadership and management

Multimedia Officer
Marketing - Port Moresby, NCD
ORGANIZATIONAL CONTEXT:
The Institute of Business Studies (IBS), from its’ humble beginning in 1987 as an arm of Nades & Associates primarily providing revision classes for the needs of Papua New Guinea Institute of Accountants (now CPA PNG), has evolved into a private University level Institution over the last thirty-four years. It has elevated as a University in January 2017 and offering its own degree programmes in the fields of Accounting & Finance, Business & Management, Economics & Development Studies and Information Technology.
Today we are one of the largest business schools in the country and continue to grow into the future. These successes are the fruits of our dedicated team member’s commitment to making a difference in Papua New Guinea through their efforts in helping educate fellow citizens.
The University is affiliated with the Southern Cross University (SCU) of Australia since 1999 and offers its degree programmes in Accounting, Business, and Information Technology. The affiliation with Southern Cross University has made IBS the first and only Institution to offer internationally recognised Bachelor programmes face to face in Papua New Guinea.
We strive to be the pioneer institution for business education in PNG. Some of our accomplishments to date are listed below:
Only educational Institution to operation a Career Centre.
Only the organisation has a “Centre of Excellence” for Leadership & Management Development.
Only private University established as per the decision of NEC and Gazettal.
Only private Institution to hold the status of “Study Centre – for the University of Papua New Guinea.” Till 2016 for 22 years.
Examination Centre for the majority of Australian & NZ Universities.
Test Centre for ICDL, Pearson VUE & Prometric.
First, publish bi-annual Journal of Business & Research in Papua New Guinea.
Accredited professional bodies in PNG & Australia and ISO 9001:2015 certified University.
Job Description:
The employee will be responsible for creating visually compelling designs while also contributing to the marketing efforts of the organization. Your role will involve blending artistic creativity with strategic marketing objectives to effectively communicate messages, promote brand awareness, and drive engagement.
Key Responsibilities:
Design Creation:
Develop high-quality visual designs for various marketing materials such as brochures, flyers, posters, banners, social media graphics, advertisements, website elements, videos and animations.
Use graphic design software and tools to create appealing layouts, illustrations, and artwork that align with brand guidelines and marketing objectives.
Ensure designs are innovative, eye-catching, and resonate with the target audience.
Branding:
Assist in maintaining brand consistency across all marketing channels and materials.
Work closely with the management team to conceptualize and execute branding initiatives, including logo design, color schemes, and typography.
Content Creation:
Collaborate with the content team to develop visual content for digital marketing campaigns, including infographics, videos, and animations.
Translate marketing concepts and messaging into visually engaging graphics and imagery.
Marketing Support:
Contribute to the development of marketing strategies and campaigns by providing creative input and design expertise.
Assist in the production and execution of marketing campaigns across various channels, including print, digital, and social media.
Monitor and analyze the performance of marketing materials and campaigns, making recommendations for optimization based on data insights.
Qualifications:
Bachelor's degree / Diploma / Certificate in Graphic Design, Marketing, or a related field.
Proven experience (5 years) working as a graphic designer, preferably in a marketing or advertising agency.
Proficiency in the following design software;
Image editing: Adobe Creative Suite (Photoshop, Illustrator, InDesign), and Canva
Video editing: Adobe Premier Pro / Adobe After Effects
Animation Creation: Autodesk 3Ds Max / Autodesk Maya / Adobe Animate
Strong understanding of marketing principles and the ability to translate them into visually appealing designs.
Excellent creative and artistic skills, with a keen eye for detail and aesthetics.
Strong communication and collaboration skills, with the ability to work effectively in a team environment.
Ability to manage multiple projects simultaneously and meet deadlines in a fast-paced, dynamic environment.
This position offers an exciting opportunity for a creative individual with a passion for both graphic design and marketing to make a significant impact on the organization's branding and promotional efforts.

The Opportunity:
As a Branch Manager, you will oversee the daily operations, sales, and service efforts of the branch, focusing on Information and Communications Technology (ICT) business software, networking, hardware, furniture, appliances, and other business services. This role requires an experienced manager with strong leadership abilities, excellent organizational skills, and a keen understanding of sales, customer service, and operational efficiency. You will ensure that the branch meets performance goals, customer satisfaction standards, and financial targets.

Team Leadership and Development

Conduct regular performance reviews and identify training needs.
Promote safety, compliance, and ethical conduct within the branch.
Customer Relationship Management
Foster strong customer relationships and ensure exceptional service.
Address client inquiries and complaints, ensuring timely and satisfactory resolution.
Regularly gather and respond to customer feedback to improve services and products.
Reporting and Compliance
Prepare and submit regular performance, financial, and operational reports.
Ensure the branch complies with all company policies, regulations, and legal standards.

Duties and Responsibilities
Branding & Content Creation
–    Produce content across digital and print channels including video, photography, social media posts, articles, and promotional materials for use across all business functions.
–    Shoot and edit short-form video content, reels, and vlogs for social media — including coverage of property launches, construction milestones, food and beverage activations, school events, and community programs.

–    Keep the company's content library organised and up to date — photos, videos, graphics, and written assets.

27800.description:
Summary
This position is responsible for managing the financial and contractual aspects of construction projects from planning to final handover. The role involves detailed cost estimation, tender preparation, contract administration, and project closeout, ensuring value for money and compliance at every stage.
Duties and Responsibilities
1. Pre-Construction Stage (Planning, Cost Estimation, and Contract Preparation)
Prepare feasibility studies and cost plans to assess project viability.
Develop preliminary and detailed cost estimates, covering material, labour, and associated costs.
Draft and finalize Bills of Quantities (BOQ), Bills of Materials (BOM), take-offs, and tender documents.
Evaluate subcontractor bids and participate in tender clarifications.
Support negotiation and drafting of contracts with vendors and subcontractors.
Propose cost-saving strategies and implement value engineering initiatives.
Ensure adherence to local regulations, statutory requirements, and internal standards.
2. Construction Stage (Contract Administration, Cost Control, and Monitoring)
Review and verify progress claims, variations, and change orders.
Perform on-site inspections and quantity validations of completed works.
Prepare and issue interim payment certificates on a regular basis.
Coordinate with project and site teams to track budgets and cost forecasts.
Negotiate adjustments for variations and update cost projections.
Manage claims, disputes, and contractual communication with external parties.
3. Post-Construction (Final Accounts and Closure)
Compile final accounts and close-out documentation for each project.
Approve final subcontractor and supplier claims.
Ensure retention release and processing of all contractually required deductions.
Assist in finalizing any pending contractual or financial issues.
4. Completion & Handover
Support final project handover activities and checklist completion.
Ensure receipt of all warranty documents, maintenance manuals, and as-built records.
Facilitate final regulatory approvals and statutory compliance certifications.
Job Requirements
Degree in Quantity Surveying, Civil Engineering, or Construction Management.
5–10 years’ experience in project cost control and contract administration.
Proficiency in tendering, cost planning, and post-contract activities.
Skilled in contract negotiation and commercial risk management.
Experience with construction measurement and cost software.
Strong leadership and team coordination capabilities.
Ability to manage multiple tasks under tight deadlines.
Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills.

27879.description:
Job Type:
Permanent
About us
K92 Mining Limited are the owners the high-grade Kainantu Gold Mine in Eastern Highlands Province. Since commencing operations in 2016, we have delivered consistent production growth. More importantly, we have contributed significantly to the economy of Papua New Guinea, more than 90% of our employees and contractors are from PNG and our local education and skills development initiatives which include scholarships, traineeships and adult literacy programs continue to bring significant benefit the communities in which we operate.
We are now transforming the operation with a new 1.2 mtpa process plant as well as extensive construction and expansion across site that will see us triple the output from our mine by 2027. In addition to our ongoing production success, we have an extensive exploration programme across our highly prospective tenement, making K92 a great place to build a long-term career.
About the role
To operate Travel buses and light vehicles in accordance with the approved travel schedule, Daily Staff Movement (DSM), to transport company personnel and others as may be directed, in a safe and efficient manner.
Key Accountabilities
Key accountabilities of this position include.
Undertake the safe handling of buses and light vehicles in transporting employees to and from work as required by the DSM.
Operate buses or other vehicles in accordance with K92 safety procedures.
Conduct a daily inspection of the allocated vehicle and ensure that it is fully serviceable and safe to operate. Notify maintenance of any defects requiring attention.
Assist to drive and influence proactive safety behaviors within workgroups through visible leadership.
About You
To be considered for this role, it is essential that you must obtain a minimum qualification of Grade 10 or above with three (3) years’ experience in operating buses, trucks and light vehicles. In addition to this, you will have some or all the following.
Possess current Class six (6) driver’s license.
A minimum of Grade 10 education.
Experience in driving Madang – Lae highway.
You must maintain a personal focus on safe vehicle operation.
You must be of sober habits and able to work with minimum supervision.
Life at K92
K92 is an Equal Opportunity Employer, our commitment is to respect the rights of every individual to work to their highest potential, free from discrimination.  Our values of Collaboration, Accountability, Respect for others, Excellence and Safety are at the core of everything we do, and they are the foundation upon which our success has been built.
Our camp is well managed and provides residents with good, healthy meals made from locally sourced fresh produce as well as internet, cable tv and a gymnasium.
At K92, we want all employees to share in our success, so as well as a competitive salary, employees also participate in our long- and short-term incentive plans, we also provide employees with access to savings incentive programs, medical assistance and the option to salary sacrifice for certain expenses.
In addition to all of this, employees can also access our Wellbeing and employee assistance programs whilst working a friendly roster.
THIS POSITION IS OPEN ONLY TO
CANDIDATES WHO RESIDE IN EASTERN HIGHLANDS AND MOROBE PROVINCES
Apply

28164.description:
PNG Air is the largest privately-owned airline company in Papua New Guinea boasting a fleet of ATR 72-600 / ATR 42-600 series aircrafts. PNG Air is one of the largest domestic airline operators in Papua New Guinea with extensive operations in the domestic network. PNG Air is now hiring for;
GENERAL MANAGER CAMG
An opportunity has risen within the CAMG Division based in Port Moresby. The General Manager CAMG is to recognize safety as a core value in all decision making involving continuing airworthiness of the PNG Air fleet. Also putting the safety management plan into effect as it applies to continuing airworthiness activities.
The General Manager CAMG will be responsible to the Chief Executive Officer for the following key areas:
Maintenance Control
Ensuring PNG Air aircraft and installed equipment are maintained in accordance with a PNG CASA approved customized maintenance programme established in accordance with the procedures in the Continuing Airworthiness Management Manual.
Ensuring the availability of aircraft for required maintenance through liaison with Airline Operations and the CEO.
Creating and maintaining MELs for aircraft types and ensuring MEL conditions and limitations are adhered to through a monitoring process.
Ensuring all discrepancies are assessed for impact on airworthiness, any deferrals correctly recorded, and where applicable categorized as defects and rectified accordingly.
Ensuring the standards and procedures specified in the aircraft maintenance programs are adhered to, all maintenance is correctly certified and aircraft are released to service after maintenance.
Ensuring all modifications and repairs are embodied in accordance with approved data and complete and accurate records are maintained in the system of aircraft logbooks.
Ensuring all applicable flight records, logs and documents are made available to PNG Air MRO and other contractors to support required maintenance.
Establishing the maintenance status of any leased aircraft and providing associated records to the maintenance provider.
Ensuring external maintenance providers are provided with or have access to, the relevant portions of the current Exposition.
Ensuring PNG Air MRO and any external maintenance provider holds or is provided with, copies of relevant manufacturers maintenance manuals.
Ensuring applicable Airworthiness Directives are accomplished.
Ensuring continuing airworthiness data which is assessed by Technical Services as appropriate for action by PNG Air, in the form of Service Bulletins and similar, is acted upon, including consequential changes to maintenance programs.
Varying maintenance programs where service experience supports a variation.
Authorising extensions to B and C category MEL items.
In liaison with the Chief Executive Officer and General Manager Safety & Quality regularly reviewing the effectiveness of internal and external maintenance agreements.
Providing advice to the Chief Executive Officer on matters relating to airworthiness.
Forecasting and Planning
Managing systems necessary to plan and ensure accomplishment of required maintenance so that airworthiness limitations are not exceeded, including rectification of defects, embodiment of modifications and repairs, and compliance with airworthiness directives.
Providing reports on projected maintenance for management perusal.
Ensuring required maintenance is notified to maintenance providers in the form of Work Packs with the optimum prior notification.
Ensuring peak operational demands are taken into account in long range forecasting of maintenance.
Ensuring close liaison between Continuing Airworthiness planning and Part 145 production planning.
Regulatory Compliance and Approvals:
Issuing Special Flight Permits in accordance with the CASA approved continuing authorization.
Ensuring aircraft are withdrawn from service when required maintenance has not been accomplished and cannot be deferred.
Liaising directly with the Civil Aviation Safety Authority on matters relating to the airworthiness of the PNG Air fleet.
Preparing amendments to the Continuing Airworthiness Manual as required.
Controlling the production and distribution of copies of the Continuing Airworthiness Management Manual and aircraft MELs.
Liaising with the Regulatory Compliance & Safety Advisor on matters concerning regulatory compliance.
Implementing any corrective and preventative actions resulting from audits of the continuing airworthiness management function.
Holding in secure storage original certificates and approvals pertaining to the airworthiness of aircraft.
Aircraft Records:
Managing the airworthiness control elements of the applicable maintenance tracking software in regard to the status of aircraft, engines and components, periodic inspections, scheduled and unscheduled special inspections, component finite and overhaul lives and other maintenance events specified in the maintenance programme.
Ensuring aircraft logbooks are maintained accurately in the prescribed manner.
To be considered, you must have the relevant qualifications, skills, knowledge and experience:
5 years Technical Experience
3 years in experience in a supervisory position
Demonstrate clear knowledge and understanding of the maintenance parts of the company’s exposition and the applicable maintenance provisions of CA Rule Part 121
Hold or have held LAME license
General Airline experience with thorough knowledge in airline commercial/private operations.
Must demonstrate excellent leadership quality
Must Demonstrate clear knowledge and understanding of planning and cost controls.
To Apply
To apply for this job simply click on the blue "Apply" button below.  If you prefer to use email instead, please send your CV and other relevant documentation to
[email protected]
.  Please include the Job ID "
#28164
" in the email's subject to ensure your application is processed.
Apply

Encourage collaboration within the School and between the School and other units of the University.
Resources

Students

Lead and support the professional development of the staff of the School.

Ensure that policies and practices within the School promote equal opportunity and equity.
Ensure environmental health and safety within the School.

Pacific Adventist University (PAU) is owned and operated by the South Pacific Division of the Seventh-day Adventist Church. The role involves significant contributions to curriculum and course development, subject coordination, and the performance of administrative responsibilities within the school. The role is also expected to actively engage in scholarly, research, and professional activities, providing leadership in advancing academic excellence, research outcomes, and the overall reputation of the School and University.

Deliver learning experiences for students in a variety of settings which may include lectures, seminars, tutorials, practical/laboratory classes, demonstrations, workshops, field excursions, and clinical sessions.

Contract Duration:
One (1) year with possible extension depending on funding
Contract type:
Full-time

Program
Location:
Kimbe, West New Britain
Reporting to:
Provincial Program Manager

WNBPHA & Other Stakeholders
Australian Doctors International (ADI) is an Australian not-for-profit organisation with more than 25 years of experience delivering community-based health programs in rural and remote Papua New Guinea. ADI works across six provinces under a Memorandum of Understanding with the PNG National Department of Health, in partnership with Provincial Health Authorities and local communities.
ADI is accredited by the Australian Government Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade (DFAT) under the Australian NGO Cooperation Program (ANCP) and is a signatory to the ACFID Code of Conduct. Our work is funded through a mix of government, corporate, philanthropic and individual donor income, and our reputation with those donors rests on delivering what we promise and reporting on it accurately and on time.
ADI HEO will work as part of a multidisciplinary team providing clinical and preventative health care services to rural communities during regular outreach patrols. The ADI HEO will also maintain an important focus on building the clinical capacity of rural health workers through case-based training and group training whilst on patrol.
This role will ensure the principles of GEDSI are applied to the entire approach in implementing policies and procedures
Responsibilities:
Lead role in planning and implementation of health outreach patrols with ADI/PHA Integrated Patrol Team
Engages with PHA regarding clinical and public health matters
Provides clinical leadership on patrols to Nursing Officers, CHWs and other patrol personnel
Provides clinical treatment with case-based teaching on patrol and in rural clinics consistent with PNG’s Standard Treatment Manuals
Delivers prevention information and awareness sessions on patrols and other times as required
Oversee and manage ADI medical supplies and equipment for patrols
Support patrol team in decision making, overseeing patrol members and cash management
Attend patrol reporting including patrol summary and logistics reports
Support rural health clinics to enter health service patrol data
Provide technical and clinical support to ADI team members
Other tasks as requested by the Manager.
Selection Criteria
Bachelor’s degree in health and or related field (preferably a midwife or HEO).
Currently registered with PNG Medical Board
High level competence in family planning, emergency obstetrics care as well as other areas in the health field
Strong understanding of underlying of determinants of health in PNG, and knowledge of mainstreaming of gender and social inclusion in health programs
Strong communication and facilitation skills
Strong analytical thinking and research skills
4-5 years hands on demonstrated experience in health programs
Proven ability to complete full training cycle (assess needs, plan, develop, coordinate, monitor and evaluate)
Advanced organizational skills with the ability to handle multiple assignments
Excellent interpersonal and communication skills
ADI’s commitment to its duty of care is reflected in its Child Safeguarding Policy and Child Safeguarding Code of Conduct promoting the protection and safety of children. ADI’s policy and code of conduct establishes internal measures to prevent and respond to child abuse and exploitation in its programs and operations across PNG.
ADI aims to integrate disability inclusion into all aspects of its programs as it strives to reach those marginalised by location, health and gender.
ADI has a zero tolerance towards sexual exploitation, abuse, and harassment in all forms. ADI’s policy covers this as well as the team’s shared responsibility on behaviour; reporting mechanisms and victim safety. ADI seeks to make the work place free from all forms of harassment, bullying and discrimination.  ADI is an Equal Opportunity Employer. ADI prohibits Online Grooming, Transactional Sex and Fraternization while engaged in any ADI business.
Any employee being investigated for breeches of ADI’s Safeguarding Policies will be suspended and/or transferred. Disciplinary measures include immediate termination for any employee found guilty of such offences.
We adhere to the ADI Code of Conduct, Our Values, ACFID Code of Conduct and the PSEAH Policy as outlined by DFAT.

27897.description:
Job Type:
Permanent
About us
K92 Mining Limited are the owners the high-grade Kainantu Gold Mine in Eastern Highlands Province. Since commencing operations in 2016, we have delivered consistent production growth. More importantly, we have contributed significantly to the economy of Papua New Guinea, more than 90% of our employees and contractors are from PNG and our local education and skills development initiatives which include scholarships, traineeships and adult literacy programs continue to bring significant benefit the communities in which we operate.
We are now transforming the operation with a new 1.2 mtpa process plant as well as extensive construction and expansion across site that will see us triple the output from our mine by 2027. In addition to our ongoing production success, we have an extensive exploration programme across our highly prospective tenement, making K92 a great place to build a long-term career.
About the role
Joining our supply team, you will manage supplier performance and provide the timely purchasing and procurement of goods delivered on time according to specified quantity, quality and cost requirements and within the supply policy guidelines. In addition, you will effectively work with the processing department to resolve continual improvements through logistics chain
Key Accountabilities
Key accountabilities of this position include.
Purchase and ensure that the quality of goods and materials purchased is to K92 Mining standards and specifications.
Recommend sources for supply of goods and services, and obtain quotations from suppliers
Analyse quotes provided for quality against specification, price, timely delivery and innovation and select the best value supplier
Ensure purchasing at the optimal price in relation to quality, quantity and delivery method.
Issue Purchase Orders that follow K92 Mining policies and standards
Ensure appropriate documentation is completed and filed for all transactions.
Manage the supplier base ensuring high level supplier performance and cost management through regular contact with suppliers.
Develop an understanding of the supply market and ensure well documented cost management.
Review performance of key suppliers across KPIs including price competitiveness, lead time compliance, delivery completeness & number of discrepancies
Investigate discrepancies and identify opportunities in the procure to pay process.
Investigate invoice discrepancies to ensure suppliers are paid in a timely manner.
Investigate PO and goods receipt discrepancies to ensure that goods are available on site to meet requirements
Recommend procure to pay process improvements in conjunction with systems enhancements
Encourage site users to follow Supply processes and reinforce the correct process where required
Ensure the timely completion of all purchasing requests.
Regular communication with internal customers to understand expectations and required timeframes when issuing purchase orders.
Follow up with suppliers to understand delays in quoting and seek alternative quotes as required
Ensure purchase requests are converted to purchase orders and issued to suppliers in a timely manner.
Manage out of hours purchase needs.
Monitor the delivery of goods and materials ensuring conformation that deliveries are completed to the K92 Mining schedules and plans.
Communicate with suppliers to ensure that specified delivery timeframes are met.
Seek alternative suppliers, logistics solutions or substitute products where emergency requirements or supplier failure may lead to goods not being available on site on the date required
Participate in the planning of shutdown maintenance and project work to ensure the availability of goods during periods of unusual demand.
Ensure Safety, Health and Environmental legislation is recognised in all purchasing activities.
About You
To be considered for this role, it is essential that you have all or the following
Minimum 3 years’ experience in industry with relevant experience in logistics
Understanding of ERP systems (Pronto) to support purchasing and expediting processes.
Competence in operation of materials handling equipment. (Eg: Forklift truck/Light truck licence)
Understanding of purchasing strategies, supplier evaluation and selection tools and their interaction with other supply processes.
Ability to draft and compile quote request.
Negotiation skills and understanding of negotiation techniques.
Commercial analysis and evaluation.
Communicate with stakeholders
Enforce strict adherence to safety standards
Protect brand image and reliability
Foster growth-friendly supply chain practices
Experience communicating with vendors in PNG and Internationally to expediting according to T&C’s for supply to K92
Ability to communicate clearly with people at all levels of the organisation and engage all relevant stakeholders.
Life at K92
K92 is an Equal Opportunity Employer, our commitment is to respect the rights of every individual to work to their highest potential, free from discrimination.  Our values of Collaboration, Accountability, Respect for others, Excellence and Safety are at the core of everything we do, and they are the foundation upon which our success has been built.
Our camp is well managed and provides residents with good, healthy meals made from locally sourced fresh produce as well as internet, cable tv and a gymnasium.
At K92, we want all employees to share in our success, so as well as a competitive salary, employees also participate in our long- and short-term incentive plans, we also provide employees with access to savings incentive programs, medical assistance and the option to salary sacrifice for certain expenses.
In addition to all of this, employees can also access our Wellbeing and employee assistance programs whilst working a friendly roster.
THIS POSITION IS OPEN ONLY TO CANDIDATES WHO HAVE THE RIGHT TO LIVE & WORK IN PNG WITHOUT SPONSORSHIP
Apply

Job Description
The Learning & Development Coordinator will enhance the skills, knowledge, and performance of employees within World Vision Papua New Guinea through the development and execution of learning and development strategies that align with the organisation's goals and objectives.
The role is responsible for developing the National Office Talent Programs in accordance with Regional Guidelines, compiling and executing the Annual Capacity Building Plan for WV PNG in collaboration with SMT and Department Heads, ensuring Learning & Reflection plans are in place for Area Programs and the National Office, and conducting workshops and trainings on P&C, organisational development and change management.
The position will manage the Talent Pool — tracking candidate progress, developing Individual Development Plans with managers, and managing SAP Academy nominations — while working with the Regional Learning and Development Advisor on regional L&D initiatives. The role will also drive staff engagement and wellbeing, including the Our Voice Survey roll-out, quarterly action-point updates for SLT, and staff care initiatives in coordination with the Regional Staff Care and Calibra teams.
The Learning & Development Coordinator will ensure an effective staff orientation program is in place for all new staff, and will support the full performance management (PFP) cycle — timely submission of agreements and end-of-year reviews, refresher trainings for staff and managers, and the calibration process to ensure final ratings are updated in Workday.
The role will act as the focal point for P&C Learning & Development needs in the National Office, engaging with SMT, managers and staff across the National Office and Area Programs, participating in partnership and regional forums, and engaging external training providers and partner organisations for cross-learning, while providing direct supervision to staff.
Educational Qualification/Skills, Knowledge & Experience
A minimum of at least 3 years' experience in all areas of P&C management and staff development.
A Bachelor's Degree or equivalent.
P&C Professional certification.
Direct experience in facilitating organisational change and P&C interventions.
At least two years' P&C work experience in a country office.
Direct experience in working with multicultural teams.
Proven ability to develop people in a cross-cultural setting.
Training and development experience.
A thorough understanding of all areas of Human Resource Management and the integration of each function.
Knowledge of WVI Partnership P&C minimum standards and practices.
Strong strategic thinking, organisational, facilitation, consultancy, change management and leadership skills.
Competent in the use of Microsoft Office computer programs including Word, Excel and PowerPoint.
Certified Trainer will be an added advantage.
Demonstrated collaboration and team building skills.
Excellent oral and written English communication skills.
Ability to travel at least 25% per month.

28146.description:
About Us
New Porgera Limited (NPL) is a leading mining company dedicated to sustainable practices and community engagement in Papua New Guinea. As the operator of the Porgera Gold Mine, we focus on extracting high-quality mineral resources while prioritizing the well-being of our employees, the environment, and the local communities. Our commitment to safety, innovation, and responsible mining ensures that we not only contribute to the economy but also support the development and prosperity of the regions we operate in. At NPL, we strive to create a positive impact, fostering strong relationships with stakeholders and promoting sustainable growth for future generations.
NPL now has a vacancy for a qualified and experienced individual to join our OH &S Department as
Officer - Emergency Response (240660)
About the role
Are you an Emergency Response Professional with theoretical training but not much practical experience? Do you want more ‘hands on’ experience in both Surface and Underground Mining Operations? Do you want to test your skills? Do you want to learn more? If so, the Porgera Mine is for you! We have a dynamic team established, new fire trucks and equipment on order and Australian Recognized Training available for the right candidate! We are after someone who is fit, energetic and enthusiastic about their professional, is this you?
Reporting to the Foreman - Emergency Response, this role will support the effective delivery of Emergency Services to the Porgera Mine. If you meet the below criteria we would like to hear from you.
In this role, you will:
Participate as an effective Emergency Response team member in all training and emergencies on the surface and underground operations
Operate emergency response equipment and vehicles situated at Porgera Mine in the event of any emergency
Participate in routine inspections of emergency equipment including fixed fire systems
Maintain a high level of health, safety and environmental awareness and comply with all relevant NPL policies & procedures.
About You
To succeed in this role, the ideal candidate will possess the following qualifications and experiences:
Minimum 5 years’ experience in the PNG Fire Service, PNG Aviation Fire Service or PNG Resources Industry in an Emergency Response role.
Knowledge and experience in operating fire appliances, SCBA, vehicle extrication equipment, firefighting & rope rescue techniques, first aid certification and command and control
Certificate 3 in Mine Emergency Response and Rescue (or equivalent)
Underground Mines Rescue Experience/Qualification (desirable)
A valid and current PNG Police Clearance with no criminal record (acquired within the last 6 months)
No history of domestic violence or workplace harassment
Grade 10 qualification or higher
The ability and willingness to train and develop within the Emergency Response Role
Current PNG Driver’s License, Class 3 and Class 6 are essential
Ability to pass a medical assessment and a rigorous fitness assessment
Mobilisation Requirement
This is a PNG National position, a site-based role on a FIFO arrangement with a rotation of 21 days on and 14 days off. Candidates must successfully pass a pre-employment medical, including drug and alcohol screening (to be arranged only for successful candidates after the interview stage), and provide an up-to-date Police Clearance Certificate (acquired within the last 6 months). Candidates must be PNG Nationals and available to start immediately. Females are encouraged to apply.
Join Our Team as an Officer- Emergency Response (240660)
Embark on a rewarding career with NPL as an Officer - Emergency Response. This role offers a unique opportunity to work with a dynamic team to contribute to NPL’s success. Enjoy a balanced work schedule, competitive compensation, and a chance to develop your career and technical expertise in a supportive and professional environment.

This advert will be open until
27
th
August 2026
. If you do not hear from NPL within next two (2) weeks following the closing date, please consider your application unsuccessful for this opportunity.

28133.description:
Business Development Officer
Simberi Gold Company Limited’s operations consists of an open cut mine on the northernmost island in the Tabar group of islands in the province of New Ireland in Papua New Guinea. Our vision is to grow sustainably and create enduring, positive impacts for the people and communities touched by our operations.
Now is an exciting time for our business and for our people. We’re going through a period of significant change and are gaining momentum in transforming our business. We’re looking for people who are ready to grow through opportunity and build a bright future with us.​​
We are currently seeking a
Business Development Officer
to join our Community Relations team in a permanent full-time position at our Simberi Operation. Your work location is Simberi Island, working a 21/14 Roster from Kavieng, Rabaul, Port Moresby, Lae, Mt Hagen, Madang, Goroka, Alotau, Wapenamanda, Popondetta, Hoskins, Wewak, Vanimo, or Tabar group of Islands.
(
Locals are encouraged to apply)
.
Reporting to the Community Relations Superintendent, the primary purpose of this role is to support the development, growth, and long-term sustainability of landowner-owned businesses and enterprises linked to Simberi Mine operations. The role ensures that landowners actively participate in spin-off and supply chain business opportunities generated by mining activities, with the goal of building viable, profitable, and sustainable enterprises that can operate beyond the life of the mine.
The position plays a key role in strengthening economic empowerment, entrepreneurship, and local business participation within mine-impacted communities.
The role incumbent and manager will identify and review the specific compliance requirements of the role.
The opportunity
Technical Accountabilities
Identify, assess, and develop landowner business opportunities linked to mine operations.
Support establishment and registration of landowner-owned business entities.
Assist with business planning, operational strategies, financial modelling, budgeting, and sustainability planning.
Facilitate access to procurement, tendering, and supply chain opportunities.
Promote entrepreneurship and enterprise development within mine-impacted communities.
Develop and deliver business management, financial literacy, and compliance training programs.
Monitor and evaluate business performance and maintain accurate business development records.
Ensure supported businesses comply with legal, regulatory, procurement, environmental, and social requirements.
Maintain a compliance register of all landowner-owned businesses according to clan origin.
Prepare progress reports and identify opportunities for continuous improvement.
Scheduling Accountabilities
Coordinate and facilitate business development workshops, training sessions, and awareness programs.
Schedule mentoring and coaching activities for landowner businesses.
Coordinate engagement with government agencies, training providers, development partners, and contractors.
Monitor and report on project milestones, business performance, and development activities.
Ensure timely completion of business registration, vendor registration, and tender submission processes.
Maintain regular reporting schedules and business development tracking systems.
People Accountabilities
Build effective relationships with landowners, local business groups, and community stakeholders.
Mentor and coach emerging landowner entrepreneurs and business leaders.
Collaborate closely with Community Relations, Procurement, Supply Chain, Finance, Contracts, and operational departments.
Liaise with government agencies, NGOs, financial institutions, and development partners.
Promote ethical business practices, transparency, and good governance.
Foster community participation, economic empowerment, and long-term business sustainability.
Are you ready to come and build your future with us?
We need the best people. People who have drive, energy and are genuinely passionate about the work they do and provide a positive impact. Additionally, we need people who see a challenge as an opportunity for growth and value working with others towards a common goal.​
We would love to hear from you if you have​:
Essential
Bachelor's Degree in Business Administration, Economics, Commerce, Entrepreneurship, or a related field.
5-8 years' experience in business development, SME support, economic empowerment programs, or related fields.
Experience supporting community or landowner business development within mining, resources, development, or community-based sectors.
Strong business development and financial analysis skills.
Knowledge of SME development and entrepreneurship principles.
Strong stakeholder engagement and relationship management capability.
Training, facilitation, mentoring, and coaching skills.
Understanding of procurement and supply chain processes.
Strong written and verbal communication skills.
Ability to work effectively in remote and culturally diverse environments.
Entrepreneurial and innovative mindset.
High level of integrity and transparency.
Strong commitment to community empowerment and economic development.
Results-oriented with a sustainable development focus.
Respectful of cultural values and landowner relationships.
Desirable
Experience working with PNG landowner business systems within the mining industry.
Knowledge of community development and economic empowerment programs.
Experience in procurement, contract management, or vendor development programs.
Existing networks with government agencies, development partners, and SME support organisations.
Understanding of governance requirements for landowner companies and incorporated business entities.

and to apply for this role, please visit:

28051.description:
The Role
Reporting to the Exploration Manager, the incumbent will play a key role and lead all field teams, tasked with progressing our exploration and resource development targets from generative to resource stage. Woodlark deposit styles range from low to intermediate sulphidation with limited to data rich targets, hosted in volcanogenic terrain with complex lithologies and structural settings. This role will lead the field teams in exploration and is well suited to a field orientated senior Geologist with diverse experience in the exploration sector who wants to join a well-funded project. Possessing a real passion for exploration and a drive to find the next discovery your skills will lead and support the team to advance several exciting projects on Woodlark Island.
Safety is one of our core values at Woodlark Gold, and we expect employees to always act in a manner that seeks to enhance the safety culture and performance of our operation. Environmental stewardship and ethical conduct in exploration activities is expected.
This is a FIFO position working a roster of 4 weeks on, followed by 2 weeks off. Preferred Points of hire include Port Moresby, Lae, Mt.Hagen and Alotau.
About the Role:
Previous experience leading exploration teams and providing proficient geological support and ensuring surface exploration, trenching and drilling programs are completed efficiently and effectively.
Proven track record of successful exploration projects, including the discovery and delineation of mineral resources.
Strong technical proficiency in geological mapping, geochemistry, geophysics, and exposure to mining processes with sound interpretative skills.
Experience managing earthworks, trenching, RC and diamond drilling programs, from planning and execution to data analysis and reporting.
Working with geological and geochemical datasets to assist in interpretation of trenching and drilling results.
Providing timely, accurate and relevant drill reporting (daily, weekly, and monthly), and other internal and external parties as appropriate.
Acting for Exploration Manager and other duties as directed.
About you:
Bachelor of Science Degree in Geology.
Previous exploration experience in essential in epithermal gold and Porphyry Cu systems (desirable).
Minimum of 8 to 10 years of relevant experience in mineral exploration.
Strong leadership capacity in all aspects of exploration, from surface mapping and sampling, trenching, RC, and diamond drilling activities, QAQC implementation and control and rehabilitation.
Experience using Microsoft Office Suite and proficiency in relevant GIS (MapInfo/Discover, QGIS), digital data capture software (desirable) and 3D software. Ability to plan and manage drilling in 3D software (Micromine preferred).
Production of reports plans and sections (Micromine preferred), and assisting is presentations.
Good written and verbal communication, leadership, and interpersonal skills.
Strong communicator, analytical, critical thinking skill and willingness to make a positive improvement.
Be self-driven and motivated, willing to mentor geologists and field technicians, contribute your ideas in a positive and proactive manner, share your skills and inspiring the team.
Valid manual Driver's Licence (Class 6) with recent driving experience well regarded.
The Offer
Role is offered on a Permanent basis.
This is an excellent opportunity to work with a dynamic and motivated team of industry professionals with experience in the demands and practices of exploration leading to mining project.
Woodlark Mining is prepared to offer an attractive remuneration package in line with experience.
Short-listing for this position commences immediately, however Woodlark reserves the right to commence processing applications prior to the nominated close off date.
If you are interested in applying for this position, please send your Resume to:
[email protected]
.
To be eligible for this role you must be a
PNG National
and previous applicant for this position need not re-apply.
If your do not hear from us in 20 workdays, please consider your application as unsuccessful.
Apply

27948.description:
Take the reins of a mature, well-run risk function reporting straight to the CEO
Guide a capable existing team through the next phase of growth
Step into a rewarding role in one of PNG's most active regulatory environments
The Role
This is a rare opportunity to lead the risk function of one of PNG's most progressive financial institutions. Reporting directly to the CEO, with a dotted line to the Board Risk Committee, the Head of Risk will oversee the bank's risk management activities to ensure risks are managed in accordance with the Board's risk appetite.
The role leads a risk team including Operational Risk, Credit Risk Analysis and Investigations, and works closely with the executive team on credit, market and operational risk matters.
Key Responsibilities
Ensure the bank's compliance with prudential, statutory and regulatory requirements, including AML/CTF legislation and BPNG/FASU directions
Oversee credit, market and operational risk, including risk registers, internal controls, and remediation of identified weaknesses
Develop and monitor Key Risk Indicators to identify emerging fraud, regulatory and money-laundering risk
Manage compliance and financial crime policy, and oversee portfolio and credit risk monitoring
Champion the bank's risk culture across its governance framework
Skills, Knowledge & Experience
Undergraduate degree in a business-related discipline.
Experience across Market Analysis, Credit Analysis, Loan Structuring, Operational Risk and Treasury activities at a bank-wide level.
Comprehensive understanding of local and international financial markets, risk, competitor activity, and the lending and non-lending products available in the local market.
Superior communication and organisational skills, with a creative, outcome-focused and 'can do' approach.
Exceptional leadership and self-management skills, with strong initiative and attention to detail.
Ability to meet the Fit & Proper requirements of the Bank of Papua New Guinea.
Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.
